typography.$description: Theme-invariant. Serif (display family) is reserved for display + section headings; body/caption/legal use the sans UI family (ADR 0035).

display.$description: Hero H1, mobile-first size — Source Serif 4.

display-large.$description: Hero H1 at the desktop breakpoint — Source Serif 4.

legal.$description: Policy-page body: full 16px with relaxed leading — legal text is never set smaller than body.

half-header.$description: App-only (#34). The 'Your read / Ticker analysis' half banners — one step below heading-1, above heading-2. Source Serif 4 semibold at 1.375rem. Sits between heading-1 (1.5rem) and heading-2 (1.25rem) in the section-header scale; never used for per-section heads (those are heading-2).

ticker.$description: App-only (ADR 0340 Amdt 3, 2026-07-27). The read header's own ticker symbol — the read's single most important glance-target. Mints its own composite rather than reusing heading-1, which bakes in font.family.serif; the ticker has always been mono (tabular figures, ADR 0035's 'the one flourish the brand allows itself'), so heading-1's *size* (1.5rem) paired with mono was never expressible as one token reference. Binds font.size.700 (1.875rem) — one step above heading-1, matching the founder-approved read-studio-identity-2026-07-19.html mockup's 1.9rem literal within a token step. Weight: font.weight.semibold (600), the system's heaviest defined step — the approved mockup's CSS carried a literal 700 (bold), which this token deliberately does not follow; minting a new weight step for one consumer was judged not worth it, since mono glyphs already read heavier than serif at equal weight and size. Never used elsewhere; the 'Your Stock' etc. block-name labels bind typography.heading-2 (serif), not this token — the ticker's mono/display pairing is unique to this one element.

projection-figure.$description: App-only (ADR 0691 dp1; read-components.md §7 v3.28, supersedes ADR 0231/v2.31/v2.62). The Outlook's per-horizon leading projection FIGURE (a single price, never a band — dp1 retires the two-price row), ONE size at every breakpoint. Retuned font.size.700→.800 (30px→36px, v2.5.0) — the number is now the section's central claim rather than one of two figures sharing the row's weight, and at parity size a single number reads smaller than the band it replaced; this is the SAME step-up v2.3.0 retired as `projection-figure-lg` for the two-price band, reinstated here as the base size for the one-price figure, not a reopening of that retirement's own reasoning (that mockup was sized against a band; this one is sized against a point). **Retyped v2.6.0 (2026-08-23, founder-directed, #2638): `fontFamily` mono→serif, `letterSpacing` normal→tight (-0.02em).** The prior mono choice was justified below (superseded text kept for trail, next sentence) as protecting tabular digit alignment across the three stacked horizons; measured digit-advance widths (fontTools, all three shipped `.woff2` latin subsets) instead show serif, sans, and mono all have uniform digit-glyph widths 0–9 — the alignment invariant holds under any family, so the family became a free choice, and serif was picked to match the register of the sentence directly beneath the figure. ~~Source Code Pro semibold, tabular figures so the three stacked horizons' digits align. Normal letter-spacing deliberately, unlike display/heading-1's tight tracking — negative tracking would misalign tabular digit columns.~~ Ink is NOT baked in (bind accent-surface.on-surface at the component, same pattern as every other typography.* token) — never accent.default or a signal color, so the figure can never read as a directive. Renders inside accent-surface.container only.

horizon-label.$description: App-only (read-components.md §7/§5 v3.28, #2638, minted 2026-08-23). The Outlook horizon row's own rank/timeframe label (`NEAR · 2 WEEKS` etc.), §7 and §5 alike (§7-parity, same as the box's other shared bindings). Supersedes `typography.caption` + `font-variant-caps: all-small-caps` on both consumers — measured (fontTools) that none of the three shipped `.woff2` latin subsets carries `smcp`/`c2sc`, so the small-caps transform was synthesized from an already-uppercase string (`outlook-copy.ts`'s `HORIZON_LABELS`) and only ever shrank it (~9px effective letterforms at the superseded 12px caption size), never actually applying a caps variant. Promoted to the display family at font.size.300 (16px, one step up from caption's 14px) with a new positive-tracking step (`font.letter-spacing.wide`, 0.06em) standing in for the small-caps transform's visual job — an eyebrow register, not a caption. Founder-approved live from a four-option interactive bench alongside `projection-figure`'s own retype (`assets/outlook-type-bench-2026-08-23.html`, this doc). Ink is NOT baked in — bind accent-surface.marker at the component, unchanged from the superseded caption binding.

Promoted from prose (app-shell.md, read-held-position.md, subscribe-pricing.md, etc. each re-typed 'base ≤639px / md ≥640px / lg ≥960px' independently) — v1.0.3, mobile-installed-app.md §8. `base` has no explicit token (it is 'below md'); `md`/`lg` are the min-width values a consumer queries against.

md.$description: min-width — sitewide/app-wide breakpoint. Below this is `base`.

lg.$description: min-width — widens grid columns inside sections; never adds columns of sections (read-held-position.md §4).

touch.$description: Theme-invariant. Promoted from prose (the de-facto '44×44px minimum' independently re-asserted in auth-screens.md, settings-surface.md, broker-connect-flow.md, broker-read-only-scope.md, read-held-position.md, site-prelaunch.md, abuse-enforcement-surfaces.md) — v1.0.3, mobile-installed-app.md §8.

min.$description: Minimum interactive hit area, every button/link/control/OTP cell/radio row. Fast-cut pills keep this hit area even where the visual pill renders smaller at `base`.

layout.$description: Theme-invariant. First key of this group, v2.9.0 — Designer ruling on stock-analyst-platform#2935 (2026-08-30).

read-column-width.$description: The read column's max measure — apps/web/src/read/read-column-width.test.ts's two call sites (`.held-position-read-host`'s max-width and `.fast-cut-pair--floating`'s `calc((100vw - 44rem) / 2 …)` gutter anchor) now bind this one value instead of two independent literals held together only by a cross-stylesheet test. Minted because the value had already drifted once in production (stock-analyst-platform#2929 — the gutters were being taken out of the 44rem under border-box, rendering every desktop read 48px narrow) with no coupling at all in place at the time; per CLAUDE.md's shared-binding rule ('two elements must be identical' is a shared-binding candidate, encoded as one token, not copied literals), a token is the stronger structural fix, not merely an equally-valid alternative to a test. In this codebase a CSS custom property IS a design token (apps/web/scripts/build-tokens.test.mjs fails any var(--x) tokens.css doesn't emit) — --read-column-width is a real DTCG token, not a workaround. read-column-width.test.ts is reduced to asserting both call sites bind var(--read-column-width) rather than comparing two strings for equality. Flagged, not fixed here: OutlookBox.css's 2.2rem panel-padding mirror hit the identical wall and was left as two literals under a test — that precedent is now the outlier, not the pattern, and is worth revisiting for consistency; tracked as a follow-up, non-blocking, out of scope for this ruling.

layer.$description: Theme-invariant z-index scale (ADR 0570) — mints a named vocabulary for the five ad-hoc z-index literals in twiceover-app, values numerically identical to what already shipped (pure rename, zero behavior change). The `raised` tier ties three semantically distinct consumers (an in-page floating pair, static app chrome, a transient dropdown) by accident of who picked which number first — a known naming tension, not resolved here (see consult 0571).

raised.$description: In-flow/fixed chrome competing in the root stacking context: FastCutPair's floating pill, the masthead account-menu disclosure, the installed-context tab bar.

popover.$description: A transient overlay anchored to its trigger: FastCutPair's popover.

overlay.$description: A full-viewport modal overlay: the re-auth overlay.

elevation.$description: App-only (#34), theme-variant. Light ('Ledger'/'Studio') leans on hairline rules with restrained warm shadows at low/medium; dark elevation is primarily surface lightening (bg.surface → bg.raised) with shadows as the secondary cue. Never on path cards — elevation difference reads as ranking (spec §6.2).

low.$description: In-flow raised elements: expanders, notices. Warm-ink ~8% over paper.

high.$description: New 2026-07-19 (ADR 0340) — the Studio read-half cards (surface.personal + surface.panel), lifted off the stone canvas. Two-layer (a broad soft cast + a tight contact shadow), deliberately heavier than medium — these are the two largest, most structurally significant surfaces on the read, not an overlay. Never on path cards (unchanged rule) or anything nested inside the two half-cards themselves.

New 2026-07-19 (ADR 0340) — dark resolution of the Studio half-card shadow. Heavier than medium for the same reason as light: the near-black canvas needs real shadow depth (dark elevation elsewhere relies mainly on surface-lightening, but these cards don't lighten — they're the lightest surfaces on the screen already).

motion.$description: App-only (#34), theme-invariant. Calm: color/opacity transitions, no movement that begs attention; everything suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

fast.$description: Hover/focus color shifts, live value refreshes.

reveal.$description: Section-loader part-and-whoosh: bars sweep outward + content rises in. Between base (180ms) and slow (1200ms); the outward sweep and the vertical settle run simultaneously at this duration.

signal.$description: App-only (#34), theme-variant — a single value cannot be AA on both ivory and graphite, so positive/negative carry .light/.dark resolutions. P&L up/down — on the NUMBER only, never on chrome, cards, or paths (spec §6.2: color-grading a path reads as advice); always paired with an explicit sign — color never carries meaning alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Lives outside themes.* so the site build never emits it. Renders on: bg.canvas / bg.surface / bg.raised only (PositionSection, the only consumer, mounts exclusively in the 'Your read' personalized half). NEVER surface.panel or accent-surface.* — the impersonal half is 'identical for every reader' (read-held-position.md §The boundary); a P&L number there would be a personalization-boundary violation, not a contrast defect, so those backgrounds are excluded from this token's reachable set on purpose (consult 0203 Q1), not merely unverified. Guarded by HeldReadDocument.test.tsx asserting no signal-* class inside .held-read-document__panel.

health.$description: App-only (#34), theme-variant. Data-health marker: limited / unavailable / stale / conflicting (spec §6.8 honest degradation). Deliberately neither a signal hue nor the accent. Lives outside themes.* so the site build never emits it. Renders on: bg.canvas / bg.surface / bg.raised / surface.panel / accent-surface.container / accent-surface.pill — unlike signal.*, a data-health marker legitimately appears in the impersonal half (SectionLoader's escalation caption, HealthNotice, ErrorPanel) since 'this data is unavailable' is not personalized P&L. light.$value retuned 2026-07-10 (consult 0203/ADR 0157) to clear all six.

macro-lean.$description: App-only (#34), theme-variant. The per-signal/composite LEAN of a macro reading (supportive/cautious toward risk appetite — product-spec §7, macro-classification-contract.md SignalState), rendered on the Macro & regime fact section only. Reserved as its OWN namespace, distinct from signal.* — this is a directional ECONOMIC READING, not P&L, and must never be read as 'this position is winning/losing' or as advice (constitution: never an imperative directive). Deliberately lower-saturation than signal.positive/negative (color.olive/color.clay vs color.green/color.red) precisely so a muted lean tint cannot be mistaken for the P&L hue even before the naming distinction is read — flagged tension + human resolution recorded in lightweight-log.md 2026-07-07 and design-system.md. Always paired with its own ▲/▼/· glyph and the state word ('supportive'/'cautious'/'neutral') — color never carries the meaning alone (WCAG 1.4.1). 'Not sourced' readings use health.degraded instead (a data-availability fact, not a lean). Lives outside themes.* so the site build never emits it. Renders on: bg.canvas / bg.surface / bg.raised / surface.panel / accent-surface.container — MacroSection is an impersonal frame rendering inside the panel (corrected 2026-07-10, consult 0203/ADR 0157 §Context point 1: previously gated against bg-canvas only on the mistaken premise it sits directly on canvas) and its loading state can appear inside OutlookBox's accent-surface.container fill. All pass at both additional backgrounds (light: 6.10:1 panel / 6.40:1 container for supportive, 6.26:1 / 6.57:1 for cautious).

path-card.$description: Component tokens for the symmetric path menu (read-components.md). One set of values for ALL path cards — uniformity enforced at the token layer; a 'featured' variant cannot exist without a reviewable change here (spec §6.2). App-only (#34). Color bindings are theme-variant (.light/.dark) because the semantic tokens they mirror moved under themes.*; structural/typographic tokens (radius, padding, fonts, gap) are theme-invariant. Lives outside themes.* so the site build never emits it.

state-field.$description: ADR 0026 state-interaction field — one binding for ALL path cards (R5 gate #2 visual parity, consult 0051). Quiet secondary-text register; references only text.muted/text.secondary so signal.*/accent.*/text.primary are UNREACHABLE through this binding. Holds in the degraded render (N/A '—' in this same body style).
Dark resolution of the ADR 0026 state-interaction field — same parity + no-signal-color-reachable guarantees as light.
Theme-invariant typography for the state-interaction field (colors are under path-card.light/.dark.state-field).

accent-surface.$description: App-only (#34). **Outlook-exclusive as of ADR 0008 Amendment 2 (2026-08-29) — was the shared Paths·Outlook pair standout; the pair rule is retired.** The accent now marks which half of the read a section belongs to, not a symmetric pair: this bronze family marks the impersonal synthesis (the Outlook box) only. Paths (the personal half) takes its own navy family, `accent-surface-paths` (below) — same roles (pill/container/border), same behavior (never a signal color, never an evaluative badge), different hue, because it now marks the other side of the ADR 0007 personalization boundary rather than a co-equal navigational destination. Applied to: the Outlook box's fast-cut pill, section container, section-header marker, and popover. Minted 2026-08-29 (ADR 0008 Amendment 2 resulting work, #2925) — the Paths-side half of the accent split the retired pair rule used to share with Outlook (see accent-surface's own $description). Same roles and same behavioral rules as accent-surface (never a signal color, never an evaluative badge/label; nothing inside the section differentiated by it) — only the hue differs, and only two of accent-surface's seven roles are minted here, because Paths' own anatomy doesn't yet need the rest: no marker/on-surface/on-surface-muted key exists because nothing in the Paths menu renders text directly on this wash today (the section heading and the pill's own border/text already bind the EXISTING themes.*.accent.default — see `border` below — and path-card content sits on the neutral bg.surface fill, not on this wash); no `rule` key exists because Paths carries no internal hairline divider analogous to the Outlook box's own. Add the missing roles if and when a consumer needs them, rather than pre-minting unused steps. Values retuned from the dormant pre-ADR-0340 navy/steel accent-surface primitives (color.navy.050/100, color.steel.200/250 — sat unemitted since 0340's bronze retune) to the pale-navy wash measured in the signed mockup (chart-forward-read-v13-2026-08-29.html's own --c-nwash/--c-npill), not minted fresh. **Border is a correction, not a transcription:** the mockup's own literal border value (--c-nborder, #B9C9DF light / #35485E dark) was measured here and found to clear only 1.3–2.2:1 against canvas/container in both themes — well under the ≥3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor accent-surface's own border/marker role holds everywhere else (see accent-surface.light/dark.border above) — so it is not reused. In its place, `border` aliases the EXISTING `themes.*.accent.default` directly (not a new primitive): this is what the mockup already does for the Paths heading marker and the fast-cut pill's own border/text (`--c-navy`/`--c-navy`, not `--c-nborder`), so aliasing the semantic token here restates a choice already made in pixels rather than introducing a new one, and it cannot drift out of sync with accent.default if that token is ever retuned.
